title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index (September 2027), 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: the publisher's standing rule, restated on conference-board.org/topics/consumer-confidence fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 332,031 bytes) -- "The Conference Board publishes the Consumer Confidence Index (R) at 10 a.m. ET on the last Tuesday of every month." 2027-09-28 is the last Tuesday of September 2027. The rule is corroborated for SEPTEMBER specifically by three of the publisher's own dated next-release lines, each read this session off an August edition fetched direct 2026-09-06 at HTTP 200 and verified against its own "Source: August <year> Consumer Confidence Survey" line rather than trusted by slug: CCI-August-2022 (883,112 bytes) "The next release is Tuesday, September 27 at 10 AM ET", CCI-August-2023 (1,254,077 bytes) "Tuesday, September 26", CCI-Aug-2024 (883,880 bytes) "Tuesday, September 24th" -- each of which is the last Tuesday of its September. A fourth September, 2026-09-29, is the next release named on the publisher's current landing page and is likewise the last Tuesday of its month. Verified after the fact for one year: CCI-Sep-2024 (517,680 bytes, "Source: September 2024 Consumer Confidence Survey") did release on 2024-09-24 as its August predecessor announced. INDEPENDENTLY DATED BY A SECOND PUBLISHER: fhfa.gov/data/hpi (HTTP 200, 89,663 bytes, fetched direct 2026-09-06) posts a "2027 HPI Release Dates" table listing "Tuesday, September 28 | Monthly Index | July 2027" -- one of twelve 2027 rows, all twelve of which match this chain's rule-derived last Tuesdays. That corroborates the calendar arithmetic, not the Conference Board's intentions. No September-2027 announcement exists yet, so this is the publisher's rule applied forward against a verified September record rather than a posted date. Discovered during the consumer-confidence-2027-08-31 initial research, checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the consumer-confidence-2027-08-31 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), one edition forward on the same chain. Proposed rather than skipped because the September print is where two open questions this session left behind get resolved, not because the chain should keep rolling. FIRST, IT IS THE SCORING VENUE FOR THIS SESSION'S OWN 80-THRESHOLD FINDING. The August lane established that TWO of this chain's Expectations readings flipped side on revision -- CCI-Aug-2024 revised July 2024 from a first-printed 78.2 up to 81.1, a year after CCI-July-2023 restated June 2023's 79.3 as exactly 80.0 -- and concluded the threshold is not readable off a first print at all. The September 2027 edition is the document that restates August 2027, so it is where that rule is tested rather than argued. SECOND, IT IS THE ONLY PLACE THE JACKSON HOLE QUESTION CAN BE ANSWERED. The August lane found that the August panel closes 6-9 days before its release (lags 7/9/6, the longest in the chain) and therefore cannot hear the last week of August -- the week the KC Fed symposium falls in -- but could source only ONE year (jackson-hole-2026-08-28) because kansascityfed.org timed out twice, so it registered a dated question rather than a pattern. A September edition fields entirely after the symposium and is the first document that can carry its effect. THREE CAUTIONS FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS. (1) September's own cut-off lag is measured for exactly one year -- CCI-Sep-2024 states "the cutoff date for the preliminary results was September 17, 2024" against a 09-24 release, a 7-day lag -- and this chain's standing rule is that the lag varies BETWEEN months and WITHIN them, so project a range from a wider sample, never a point off that single observation. (2) The September print sits INSIDE the 2027 FOMC blackout (Sep 4-16 is the decoded window and the 09-14/15 meeting follows it), unlike the August print, which is the only 2027 CB print in a blackout-free month -- so the two are not interchangeable on Fed-transmission questions. (3) September CB days are clean 5 of 5 in the tape window, so the August lane's null control (July colliding vs August clean, 0 of 9) can be re-run against a second clean month for the out-of-sample n it explicitly said it lacked at n=6. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
